natanael: hey team :wave: i'm natanael (started today) — trying to build the inference runtime from source on an ubuntu 22.04 dev VM (gcc 12, cuda-12.1) and i'm hitting linker errors. any pointers on what i should check? who do i cc for infra setup?
paige: welcome! :rocket: ping eng-runtime here. can you paste the exact linker output and nvcc --version? also check the onboarding doc in #devex for infra steps.
natanael: sure — here's the top of the failure (cmake + ninja):
```
[100%] Linking CXX executable bin/runtime_server
/usr/bin/ld: build/_deps/libcuda/lib/libcudart.so: undefined reference to `cublasCreate_v2'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```
nvcc --version: "Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105"
paige: thanks. that looks like a missing libcublas at link time or a mismatched driver/toolkit. liam or miriam — any quick checks? :eyes: 
liam: most likely driver vs toolkit mismatch or your LD_LIBRARY_PATH doesn't include the cublas location. run `nvidia-smi` to see driver, then `ldd bin/runtime_server` to see where libraries resolve. also confirm CMAKE picked /usr/local/cuda-12.1.
natanael: ran nvidia-smi: "Driver Version: 535.54" (looks recent). here's ldd on the binary (trimmed):
```
libcublas.so.12 => not found
libcudart.so.12 => /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart.so.12
libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1
```
miriam: yep that matches — libcublas is either missing from LD_LIBRARY_PATH or not installed. if you installed CUDA via package manager sometimes cublas will be in a separate package like `libcublas-12-1` or under `/usr/local/cuda-12.1/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/`. try `ls /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 | grep cublas` and `echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
devon: quick notes from infra: prefer installing the full CUDA toolkit (runfile) on your dev VM instead of mixing distro packages; apt packages vary by distro and split libs. if you must, `sudo apt install libcublas-12-1` is ok for dev VMs. avoid symlinking system libs into /usr/local/cuda — that can hide real mismatches. after installing, export LD_LIBRARY_PATH and run `sudo ldconfig` or add the path to /etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf. also you can add `-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 -lcublas"` as a short workaround.
natanael: i installed the missing libcublas package from the toolkit and set `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` then `sudo ldconfig`. re-ran cmake && ninja and the link finished :thumbsup: build succeeded. thanks everyone!
paige: amazing, welcome aboard and glad that fixed it. for infra onboarding and ssh/key rotation steps see: https://redwood.internal/docs/onboarding/dev-vm-setup (cc @devex). also ping me if you want pairing time with runtime folks later today. :wave:
miriam: if you run into perf regressions after this, shout here and we'll help profile.
devon: noted — i'll follow up with a short checklist in the onboarding ticket for driver/toolkit best practices. again welcome! :tada:
